text: During a short break in a long trial, the judges and lawyers of the Law Courts gathered in a private room, where one of them opened a newspaper and read aloud that Ivan Ilyich Golovin had died. <break time="0.8s" /> Upon hearing the news, each man present thought first not of the colleague he had lost but of the vacant post, and of the promotions and transfers that it might bring to himself or to his friends. <break time="0.8s" /> Beneath these calculations lay another feeling, which none of them would admit, a quiet relief that the one who had died at forty five was Ivan Ilyich and not themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> His old friend Pyotr Ivanovich went to the house that evening, and although he had meant to share the familys grief, he found himself thinking less about the dead man than about the evenings card game. <break time="0.8s" /> In the drawing room, the widow, Praskovya Fyodorovna, spoke at length of her own suffering during her husbands illness and then asked, in the same tone, how she might obtain more money from the government. <break time="0.8s" /> So absorbed was she in these practical matters that Pyotr Ivanovich, sitting awkwardly on a low stool with broken springs, began to feel that his words of comfort were hardly needed. <break time="0.8s" /> As he was leaving, he met Gerasim, the young servant who had cared for his master to the end, and Gerasim said simply that it was Gods will and that all of us must come to it one day. <break time="0.8s" /> Stepping out into the fresh night air, Pyotr Ivanovich felt as if he had escaped something unpleasant, and he hurried off, hoping that he might still be in time for the card game.
